quests.conceptTitle: Agreement: Head Noun in a Long Noun Phrase
quests.faultySentence: The proportion of graduates who secure permanent contracts within a year of leaving university have declined steadily since 2015.
quests.correctedSentence: The proportion of graduates who secure permanent contracts within a year of leaving university has declined steadily since 2015.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'the proportion', which is singular; the plural 'graduates' sits inside a modifying clause. The verb must be 'has declined'.
quests.nativeTip: Set aside the relative clause and the prepositional phrase. Which noun is the real subject, 'proportion' or 'graduates'?

quests.conceptTitle: Agreement: Singular Head Noun Before a Compound
quests.faultySentence: A combination of rising costs and shrinking demand are forcing several manufacturers to close plants.
quests.correctedSentence: A combination of rising costs and shrinking demand is forcing several manufacturers to close plants.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'a combination', which is singular. The two nouns after 'of' describe it but do not make the subject plural, so the verb is 'is forcing'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Rising costs and shrinking demand' is a list inside the phrase. What is the actual subject of the verb?

quests.conceptTitle: Agreement: Each Of with an Intervening Phrase
quests.faultySentence: Each of the seventeen recommendations included in the appendix, along with the supporting data, require approval from the full board.
quests.correctedSentence: Each of the seventeen recommendations included in the appendix, along with the supporting data, requires approval from the full board.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each of' is singular, and 'along with the supporting data' does not change that. The verb must be 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: Two things can mislead you here: a plural noun close to the verb and an 'along with' phrase. What does 'each of' need?

quests.conceptTitle: Tense and Clause Relationship: Past Perfect with Simple Past
quests.faultySentence: The negotiations had already collapsed twice before the parties finally reach an agreement in March.
quests.correctedSentence: The negotiations had already collapsed twice before the parties finally reached an agreement in March.
quests.ruleExplanation: The past perfect 'had collapsed' marks the earlier events, while the later event in the narrative takes the simple past: 'reached'.
quests.nativeTip: The earlier collapses use the past perfect. Which tense fits the later event in the same story?

quests.conceptTitle: Tense and Clause Relationship: Since with Present Perfect
quests.faultySentence: Since the software update was released, users reported far fewer login errors.
quests.correctedSentence: Since the software update was released, users have reported far fewer login errors.
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'since' plus a past starting point, the main clause describes a period that reaches the present, so it takes the present perfect: 'have reported'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Since' introduces a starting point that continues up to now. Which tense links that point with the present?

quests.conceptTitle: Tense and Clause Relationship: By the Time with Past Perfect
quests.faultySentence: By the time the inspectors arrived, the staff has already removed the damaged stock from the shelves.
quests.correctedSentence: By the time the inspectors arrived, the staff had already removed the damaged stock from the shelves.
quests.ruleExplanation: The removal was completed before the inspectors arrived, so it needs the past perfect 'had already removed', not the present perfect 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: The clause 'by the time the inspectors arrived' is in the past. Which tense shows an action completed before that moment?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Case: Whoever vs Whomever in Embedded Clauses
quests.faultySentence: The panel will award the grant to whomever they believe will make the best use of it.
quests.correctedSentence: The panel will award the grant to whoever they believe will make the best use of it.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'will make'; 'they believe' is only an insertion. Subjects take 'whoever', not 'whomever'.
quests.nativeTip: Ignore the insertion 'they believe' for a moment. Is the pronoun the subject of 'will make', or the object of something?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Case: Misused Reflexive in a Coordinated Object
quests.faultySentence: The invitation to the annual dinner was sent to my colleagues and myself.
quests.correctedSentence: The invitation to the annual dinner was sent to my colleagues and me.
quests.ruleExplanation: A reflexive pronoun needs a matching subject, and none exists here. After the preposition 'to', the plain object form 'me' is correct.
quests.nativeTip: 'Myself' needs an 'I' doing the action in the same clause. Is there one here? What object form fits after 'to'?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Agreement with the Correct Antecedent
quests.faultySentence: Having reviewed the tenders, the panel rejected the ones from the two smaller firms because it lacked technical detail.
quests.correctedSentence: Having reviewed the tenders, the panel rejected the ones from the two smaller firms because they lacked technical detail.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun refers back to 'the ones', meaning several tenders, so it must be plural: 'they lacked'.
quests.nativeTip: What lacked technical detail? Check whether that noun is singular or plural.

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Modifiers: Elliptical Clause
quests.faultySentence: Although exhausted after the flight, the meeting began on time.
quests.correctedSentence: Although exhausted after the flight, the delegates began the meeting on time.
quests.correctedPart: the delegates began the meeting on time
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Exhausted' describes people, but the subject is 'the meeting'. Naming the delegates as the subject gives the opening phrase a logical target.
quests.nativeTip: Who was exhausted after the flight? The subject after the comma should be able to feel that way.

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clause Attachment: Clause Beside Its Noun
quests.faultySentence: We hired an interpreter for the delegation who speaks four languages fluently.
quests.incorrectPart: an interpreter for the delegation who speaks four languages fluently
quests.correctedSentence: We hired an interpreter who speaks four languages fluently for the delegation.
quests.correctedPart: an interpreter who speaks four languages fluently for the delegation
quests.ruleExplanation: As written, 'who speaks four languages' follows 'the delegation'. The skill belongs to the interpreter, so the clause must come right after 'interpreter'.
quests.nativeTip: Who speaks four languages, the interpreter or the delegation? Keep the clause beside the noun it describes.

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clauses: Defining vs Non-Defining
quests.faultySentence: Employees, who arrive more than thirty minutes late, will have their pay reduced; punctual employees will not.
quests.incorrectPart: Employees, who arrive more than thirty minutes late, will
quests.correctedSentence: Employees who arrive more than thirty minutes late will have their pay reduced; punctual employees will not.
quests.correctedPart: Employees who arrive more than thirty minutes late will
quests.ruleExplanation: Commas make the clause extra information about all employees. Since only late employees are affected, the clause is defining and needs no commas.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence says punctual employees are treated differently. Do the commas make the clause apply to all employees, or only some?

quests.conceptTitle: Articles: Zero Article with General Uncountable Nouns
quests.faultySentence: Access to the clean water remains one of the most pressing challenges facing rural communities in the region.
quests.correctedSentence: Access to clean water remains one of the most pressing challenges facing rural communities in the region.
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence refers to clean water in general, an uncountable idea, so it takes no article: 'clean water'.
quests.nativeTip: Is the sentence about one specific supply of water, or about clean water as a general resource?

quests.conceptTitle: Articles: Uncountable Nouns in Formal Writing
quests.faultySentence: The government has introduced a new legislation aimed at reducing single-use plastics.
quests.correctedSentence: The government has introduced new legislation aimed at reducing single-use plastics.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Legislation' is uncountable, so it cannot take 'a' or a plural ending. Use 'new legislation' or 'a new law'.
quests.nativeTip: Can 'legislation' be counted as one, two, three? What does that tell you about 'a'?

quests.conceptTitle: Articles: A for First Mention in a Noun Phrase
quests.faultySentence: It was the first time in the country's history that voters had elected the woman as head of state.
quests.correctedSentence: It was the first time in the country's history that voters had elected a woman as head of state.
quests.ruleExplanation: No specific woman has been identified earlier, so the noun is being introduced for the first time and needs 'a', not 'the'.
quests.nativeTip: Has any particular woman been mentioned before? Which article introduces someone new?

quests.conceptTitle: Conditionals and Modals: Could Have + Past Participle
quests.faultySentence: If the shipment had arrived on schedule, we could launched the campaign in June.
quests.correctedSentence: If the shipment had arrived on schedule, we could have launched the campaign in June.
quests.ruleExplanation: A past unreal condition needs 'could have' plus the past participle in the result clause: 'could have launched'.
quests.nativeTip: The if-clause describes an unreal past situation. What verb form follows 'could' in the result clause?

quests.conceptTitle: Conditionals: Unless with Present Simple
quests.faultySentence: Unless the board will approve the additional funding, the project must be scaled back.
quests.correctedSentence: Unless the board approves the additional funding, the project must be scaled back.
quests.ruleExplanation: Conditional clauses, including those with 'unless', use the present simple for future meaning, so the sentence needs 'approves', not 'will approve'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Unless' works like 'if not'. Do conditional clauses about the future take 'will'?

quests.conceptTitle: Conditionals and Modals: Be Able To
quests.faultySentence: Were the rules to be relaxed, banks would be able hold less capital against risky loans.
quests.correctedSentence: Were the rules to be relaxed, banks would be able to hold less capital against risky loans.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Be able' is followed by 'to' plus the base verb, so the result clause needs 'would be able to hold'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Be able' needs a small connecting word before the next verb. What is missing?

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clauses and Agreement: Whose Clauses
quests.faultySentence: The engineers whose designs were selected for the final round is expected to present their prototypes next month.
quests.correctedSentence: The engineers whose designs were selected for the final round are expected to present their prototypes next month.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'the engineers', which is plural; 'whose designs were selected' only describes them. The verb must be 'are expected'.
quests.nativeTip: Which noun does 'whose designs were selected' describe? Is that noun singular or plural?

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clauses and Agreement: One of the ... That
quests.faultySentence: This is one of the few studies that has examined long-term effects in adolescents.
quests.correctedSentence: This is one of the few studies that have examined long-term effects in adolescents.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' refers back to the plural 'studies', not to 'one', so the verb in the relative clause is plural: 'have examined'.
quests.nativeTip: In 'one of the few studies that ...', what does 'that' refer back to: 'one' or 'studies'?

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clauses and Agreement: Intervening Clause
quests.faultySentence: The manager, whom the staff respect greatly, are retiring at the end of the year.
quests.correctedSentence: The manager, whom the staff respect greatly, is retiring at the end of the year.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'the manager', a single person; the relative clause about the staff does not change it. The verb is 'is retiring'.
quests.nativeTip: 'The staff' sits inside the relative clause. What is the true subject of 'retiring'?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison and Parallelism: Both ... And
quests.faultySentence: The new curriculum is both more rigorous than the old one and offers greater flexibility.
quests.correctedSentence: The new curriculum is both more rigorous than the old one and more flexible.
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'both' comes the comparative phrase 'more rigorous than the old one', so the second part should match: 'and more flexible'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Both ... and' joins matching structures. What kind of phrase follows 'both'?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison and Parallelism: Comparing Like with Like
quests.faultySentence: Housing in the capital is far more expensive than any other city in the country.
quests.correctedSentence: Housing in the capital is far more expensive than in any other city in the country.
quests.ruleExplanation: As written, housing is compared with a city. Adding 'in' compares housing in the capital with housing in any other city.
quests.nativeTip: What is being compared: housing with a city, or housing in one place with housing in another?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison and Parallelism: Not Only ... But Also
quests.faultySentence: Not only was the study larger than earlier trials, but also it lasted considerably longer.
quests.incorrectPart: but also it lasted considerably longer
quests.correctedSentence: Not only was the study larger than earlier trials, but also considerably longer.
quests.ruleExplanation: The first part is 'was larger than...', so the second part should complete the same frame: 'but also considerably longer'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Not only' opened with 'was ... larger'. What kind of phrase should follow 'but also'?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Complements: Recommend + Gerund, Parallel
quests.faultySentence: The auditors recommended reviewing the procedures and to update the training materials before the next inspection.
quests.correctedSentence: The auditors recommended reviewing the procedures and updating the training materials before the next inspection.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Recommended reviewing' is followed by a gerund, so the second item in the pair must match: 'and updating'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Recommend' takes a gerund. Should the second item in the pair match the first?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Complements: Admit + Gerund
quests.faultySentence: The applicant admitted to have submitted incomplete documents, but denied any intention to mislead the panel.
quests.correctedSentence: The applicant admitted having submitted incomplete documents, but denied any intention to mislead the panel.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Admit' takes a gerund for a completed action, so the sentence needs 'admitted having submitted', not the infinitive 'to have submitted'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Admit' is followed by a gerund when the action has already happened. Which form fits?

quests.conceptTitle: Verb Complements: Passive Require + Perfect Infinitive
quests.faultySentence: Applicants are required having completed at least two years of professional experience before they can be considered.
quests.correctedSentence: Applicants are required to have completed at least two years of professional experience before they can be considered.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Be required' is followed by an infinitive, and the perfect infinitive 'to have completed' shows the experience must come first.
quests.nativeTip: The passive 'are required' needs a particular structure after it. Which one?

quests.conceptTitle: Integrated Control: Relative Clause Agreement in a Conditional Sentence
quests.faultySentence: Had the committee been informed of the risks earlier, it would not have approved the plan, which, in retrospect, were poorly conceived.
quests.correctedSentence: Had the committee been informed of the risks earlier, it would not have approved the plan, which, in retrospect, was poorly conceived.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' refers to 'the plan', which is singular, and 'in retrospect' looks back on a finished past decision, so the verb is 'was poorly conceived'.
quests.nativeTip: What does 'which' refer to, the risks, the committee, or the plan? Then decide singular or plural.

quests.conceptTitle: Integrated Control: Inversion After a Fronted Only Clause
quests.faultySentence: Only when the funding is secured and the permits are granted construction will begin.
quests.correctedSentence: Only when the funding is secured and the permits are granted will construction begin.
quests.ruleExplanation: A fronted 'only when' clause triggers inversion, so the auxiliary moves before the subject: 'will construction begin'.
quests.nativeTip: A sentence that opens with 'only when ...' changes the order in the main clause. What comes before the subject?

quests.conceptTitle: Integrated Control: Agreement in a Long Coordinated Sentence
quests.faultySentence: In the latest survey, the number of respondents who described themselves as satisfied with public services has fallen, while the proportion of those reporting long waiting times have risen sharply.
quests.correctedSentence: In the latest survey, the number of respondents who described themselves as satisfied with public services has fallen, while the proportion of those reporting long waiting times has risen sharply.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject is 'the proportion', which is singular; 'those reporting long waiting times' only describes it. The verb must be 'has risen'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the head noun of the second subject. Is it 'proportion' or 'times'?
